title: C. STATES OF MATTER — Q61–90 (part 1)
source: Chemistry MCQ Test OPTIMIZED — C. STATES OF MATTER — Q61–90, pages 3-3 [Chemistry_MCQ_Test_OPTIMIZED.md]
textbookText: 61. The three common states of matter are distinguished mainly by differences in: A) Intermolecular forces and the degree of molecular order/freedom of motion B) Chemical composition of the substance C) Color of the substance D) Atomic number of the constituent elements

62. In the solid state, particles are: A) Closely packed in a fixed, ordered arrangement with only vibrational motion B) Free to move randomly throughout the container C) Widely spaced with negligible intermolecular forces D) Arranged with no definite pattern but strong attraction

63. In the gaseous state, intermolecular forces are: A) Very weak/negligible, allowing particles to move freely and independently B) Very strong, holding particles in fixed positions C) Exactly equal to those in the liquid state D) Responsible for a gas having a fixed shape

64. Which of these is a characteristic property unique to the liquid state (compared to solid and gas)? A) Definite volume but no definite shape (takes the shape of its container) B) Both definite shape and definite volume C) Neither definite shape nor definite volume D) Zero intermolecular forces

65. The process by which a solid changes directly to gas without passing through the liquid state is called: A) Sublimation B) Evaporation C) Condensation D) Deposition only (one-directional term, distractor)

66. Surface tension of a liquid arises due to: A) Unequal (net inward) intermolecular forces experienced by molecules at the liquid surface B) Repulsive forces between all molecules uniformly C) The liquid's boiling point D) Gravity acting only on surface molecules

67. Viscosity of a liquid is a measure of: A) Its resistance to flow, caused by internal friction between layers of the liquid B) Its ability to evaporate quickly C) Its boiling point D) Its surface tension exclusively

68. An extraordinary property of water relevant to states of matter is that: A) Solid water (ice) is less dense than liquid water, so ice floats — unusual compared to most substances B) Ice is denser than liquid water, like most substances C) Water has no measurable surface tension D) Water cannot exist in the gaseous state

69. Evaporation differs from boiling in that evaporation: A) Occurs only at the surface of a liquid, at any temperature below the boiling point B) Occurs throughout the bulk of the liquid at a fixed temperature C) Requires no energy input at all D) Only occurs at exactly 100°C for water

70. Plasma, often called the "fourth state of matter," consists of: A) Ionized gas containing free electrons and positive ions, found in stars and lightning B) A solid with extremely high density C) A liquid with zero viscosity D) A gas with no intermolecular forces and no ions

71. Which of these best explains why gases are easily compressible while solids and liquids are not? A) Gases have large intermolecular spacing, so molecules can be pushed much closer together B) Gas molecules are chemically different from solid/liquid molecules C) Gases have stronger intermolecular forces than solids D) Compressibility depends only on temperature, not spacing
72. The transition of a liquid to a solid is called: A) Freezing (solidification) B) Melting (fusion) C) Vaporization D) Sublimation

73. Amorphous solids (like glass) differ from crystalline solids in that amorphous solids: A) Lack a long-range, ordered particle arrangement and don't have a sharp melting point B) Have a perfectly ordered lattice structure and a sharp melting point C) Are always liquids at room temperature D) Have no intermolecular forces at all

74. Capillary rise of a liquid in a narrow tube is caused by a combination of: A) Cohesive forces (between liquid molecules) and adhesive forces (between liquid and tube surface) B) Gravity alone C) Atmospheric pressure alone D) The liquid's boiling point

75. Which of the following demonstrates an extraordinary fact about supercooled liquids? A) A liquid can sometimes be cooled below its normal freezing point without solidifying, remaining metastable as a liquid B) Supercooled liquids always freeze instantly at room temperature C) Supercooling is impossible for any real liquid D) Supercooled liquids have higher entropy than gases

76. Vapor pressure of a liquid at a given temperature is: A) The pressure exerted by vapor in equilibrium with its liquid in a closed container B) The pressure of the liquid itself, not its vapor C) Always equal to atmospheric pressure regardless of temperature D) Independent of temperature

77. Boiling point of a liquid is reached when its vapor pressure: A) Becomes equal to the external (atmospheric) pressure B) Becomes zero C) Exceeds the critical pressure only D) Is unrelated to atmospheric pressure
78. The state of matter with the highest degree of molecular disorder (entropy) among solid, liquid, and gas (at similar conditions) is: A) Gas B) Solid C) Liquid D) All three have equal disorder
